# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old (by the end of Volume 5)  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c27 P2](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- **Role:** Student; aspiring poet  <sub>[v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)</sub>
- **Titles:** The Genius  <sub>[v2 c5 P3](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0003), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has an unusually beautiful, delicate face with a high forehead and a halo of chestnut curls that later give way to close-cropped brown hair. He possesses deep, dark-blue eyes that reflect a meditative and imaginative nature. By sixteen, he grows tall for his age, taking after his father's stature.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P28](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0028), [v2 c23 P28](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0028), [v2 c27 P2](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0002)_

## Personality

Paul is an exceptionally imaginative, sensitive, and meditative boy who views the world with poetic wonder. Despite his deep inner life and rich dream-world, he is manly, well-liked, and capable of holding his own among other children. He possesses a gentle, loving disposition and seeks out kindred spirits who understand his unique way of thinking. He is deeply devoted to those he cares about, especially his father and his teacher.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019), [v2 c27 P33](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0033)_

- Highly imaginative and poetic  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020)</sub>
- Sensitive and thoughtful  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

## Abilities

- Poetic composition and creative writing  <sub>[v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)</sub>

## Goals

- To grow up and live with his father  <sub>[v2 c15 P10](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0010)</sub>
- To become a poet  <sub>[v2 c15 P20](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0020)</sub>

## History

Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States at age ten to live with his grandmother. He enters the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley, quickly forming a close bond with her as a kindred spirit. Throughout his schooldays, he populates his imagination with 'Rock People' and whimsical fairy-like creations. When his father, Stephen Irving, visits Avonlea, Paul helps reunite him with his former love, Miss Lavendar Lewis. Stephen and Miss Lavendar marry and eventually take Paul with them to live in Boston and later travel abroad. As he matures into a tall teenager, Paul develops his literary talent and begins writing published poetry, while maintaining an enduring affection for his former teacher.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c28 P28](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0028), [v2 c30 P10](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0010), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Born in the United States to Stephen Irving and his late wife  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- Raised by his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, in Avonlea after his mother died  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>

> I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because... I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>
